# W010 — norm-selected odd cubic concentration

2026-10-08. Parent constructive candidate, PROVISIONAL.
No experiment, installed solver, Lean change or factoring improvement.
This keeps a zero-absorbing odd polynomial, merges two signed sampled
pairs at once, and uses no reciprocal chart or power-subgroup promise.
It is a new acquisition rule; earlier polynomial/reciprocal envelopes
do not automatically apply.

## Executable mechanism

Maintain a monic odd polynomial by its circuit, initially P(X)=X.
Take two fresh uniform residues modulo a remaining N=pq, p,q>3, and
evaluate z=P(r), u=P(s). Test z,u,z-u,z+u individually by gcd.
A proper gcd returns a factor. A full failure is a paid no-op under a
fixed raw-attempt budget. On the unit chart set

    beta=z^2+z*u+u^2,
    P_new=P^3-beta*P.                                           (1)

Beta need not be a unit. There is no division or square root. An optional
gcd(beta,N) would be an additional success channel and is not included
in the initial protocol. Every current map remains monic and odd;
zero is absorbing.

The exact identity is

    F_beta(T)-F_beta(z)=(T-z)*(T-u)*(T+z+u),
    F_beta(z)=F_beta(u)=F_beta(-z-u)=-z*u*(z+u).                   (2)

Thus the two actually sampled fibers z,u merge; their distinct negatives
merge into the opposite output. The third value -z-u also merges if it
is in the current image. Its presence is not assumed or supplied as an
oracle. The legal chart ensures the two outputs are nonzero and opposite.

Each update/probe stage needs a fixed number of modular operations.
Fresh parameter acquisition through depth k still costs O(k^2), and a
probe costs O(k); odd symmetry supplies negative anchors without extra
evaluations. The proposed saving would be a faster concentration of
nonzero fibers before a final absorption step, not cheap circuit evaluation.
The final step P*(P-a), a=P(r) from one paid fresh sample, can absorb a
mass-biased fiber; its cost and CRT success remain charged.

## Exact proposed sampler and drift

Fix one current odd map over F_p. Its output law mu is symmetric.
Write m=mu(0), let nu be the nonzero residual law, and set
s=sum nu, v=sum nu^2, q4=sum nu^4. Define Q(z,u)=z^2+z*u+u^2 and

    K(beta)=sum_(z,u!=0; z!=u; z!=-u; Q(z,u)=beta) nu(z)*nu(u),
    A(beta)=sum_(a!=0; a^2=beta) nu(a)^2,
    B(beta)=sum_(a!=0; a^2=beta) nu(a).

All ordered pairs are counted. Symmetry gives
sum K=s^2-2v=:ell. This is the raw legal probability; when ell=0
the conditional acquired-parameter law is undefined. When ell>0 it is
K(beta)/ell. The sampler measures no K.

The full off-diagonal collision gain at fixed beta has three disjoint
parts: K(beta), the opposite pairs A(beta), and the pairs involving zero
2m*B(beta). Also m_new=m+B(beta).
Symmetry implies B(beta)^2=2A(beta), including beta=0 or a nonsquare,
where both sides are zero. Subtracting the new atom square yields

    v_new-v=K(beta)-A(beta),
    m_new-m=B(beta).                                            (3)

Consequently the actual raw moments are

    E[1_legal*Delta v]=sum_beta K(beta)^2-sum_beta K(beta)*A(beta),
    E[1_legal*Delta m]=sum_beta K(beta)*B(beta).                  (4)

This supplies an executable bias toward the relevant quadratic-form
merger mass. Unlike the reciprocal sampler, it does not automatically
remove the two sampled heavy fibers into marked atoms. However the
root-removal term in (4) can still defeat a gain for a weighted law.
No universal monotonicity or reachable-law persistence is asserted.

For a flat symmetric residual support of size M, mass d=s/M per point,
every legal pair forces the four distinct ordered pairs
(z,u),(u,z),(-z,-u),(-u,-z). Thus K(beta)>=4d^2, while A(beta)<=2d^2.
This gives pointwise Delta v>=2d^2. The post-update law is generally
nonflat, so this one-step property cannot be iterated without proof.

## The actual uniform start, not an idealized distribution

Let epsilon=chi(-3), h=chi(3), C=p-epsilon-4 and D=3+h.
At uniform affine input nu=1/p on F_p^*, let k_beta=p^2*K(beta).
The standard nonsingular binary-quadratic count, followed by deletion
of zero coordinates and the two diagonals, proposes

    k_0=(p-1)*(1+epsilon),
    k_beta=C-D*chi(beta),              beta!=0,
    ell=(p-1)*(p-3)/p^2.                                     (5)

One can derive the count by completing the square:
4Q(z,u)=(2z+u)^2+3u^2. It is not a heuristic random-parameter law.
At nonzero beta, the original conic has p-epsilon points; remove
2*(1+chi(beta)) zero-coordinate points, 1+chi(beta/3) diagonal points,
and 1+chi(beta) opposite points. These deletions are disjoint for p>3.

Equations (3)-(5) give the proposed exact conditional means

    E[Delta v | legal]
      =[(p-1)*(1+epsilon)^2+C^2+D^2-C+D]/[p^2*(p-3)],
    E[Delta m | legal]=(C-D)/[p*(p-3)].                         (6)

In particular the first residual collision mass is 2/p+O(1/p^2),
and root mass is 2/p+O(1/p^2). No first-step exponent gain follows.
The potential difference is the subsequent weighted quadratic incidence,
not initial formal degree three or the number of planted pairs.

## Complete acquisition and recovery obligations

At a fixed map modulo N, fresh CRT samples are independent and the joint
clean probability is ell_p*ell_q. The raw local drifts in (4) multiply by
the other prime's ell in the no-op full-tape process. The accepted histories
are correlated across primes. Zero/full gcds and all unstarted stages stay
in the ledger; a clean-law formula is not a factoring success probability.
Every intermediate zero remains an endpoint zero, but extra coefficient
or derivative gcds would change the protocol.

A cheap-looking reservoir shortcut has an explicit debt. In a fixed pool
of input samples, applying the current global update to every stored value
merges at least the two distinct sampled classes on every accepted step.
Without replenishment, a pool of M distinct values supports at most M-1
such steps; if signed pairs are stored, the drop can be larger. Updating
all M values at every stage costs O(M*k). A fresh input evaluated through
the full circuit costs O(k). This closes only that literal pool scheme;
it is not a lower bound on lazy or structurally compressed acquisition.

The decisive mathematical gate is (4) for REACHABLE weighted laws:
does its non-forced quadratic-form energy create useful concentration
soon enough to pay for the k^2 training and final probes, or is its drift
only the generic 1/p scale? An arbitrary flat support or a favorable
quadratic-form count does not establish this. A cheap exact audit should
first validate (2)-(6), seek a weighted symmetric counterexample to any
attempted monotonic extension, and isolate the forced contribution.
A depth sweep is not selected until that calculation identifies a
quantitative candidate advantage and a preregistered rejection criterion.

The scalar-product branch W008 remains separate: an improved collision
detector could save work without requiring the concentration claimed here.


Audit all (1)-(6), ordered-pair multiplicities, the zero/opposite-pair collision decomposition and beta=0 case, symmetry, clean-chart probability, and exact uniform conic counts for p>3. Confirm the pointwise flat symmetric-support gain and identify what stops its iteration. Seek one cheap exact weighted symmetric counterexample to universal nonnegative drift if available, but don't run a prime/weight search; a symbolic support with a few opposite pairs and chosen masses is allowed. Separate forced-pair contribution from other collisions in the raw squared K term; no unsupported bound may be inferred from symmetry. Return report and manifest.

# W010 — a quantitative envelope from the acquired norm law

2026-10-08. Parent derivation, PROVISIONAL pending independent review.
No candidate experiment, Lean change or complete factoring improvement.
The positive-drift theorem is accepted separately. The question here is
whether its rate is large enough to help a short sequential circuit.

## Smooth leading form and the actual norm distribution

Fix any current monic odd P in F_p[X], of formal degree D=3^j, p>3.
Its coefficients may have been chosen adaptively; freeze the whole map
before taking fresh uniform X,Y. Define

    eta(b)=Pr[Q(P(X),P(Y))=b],   Q(z,u)=z^2+zu+u^2.

This includes all pairs, not only the legal ones defining K. Thus
K(b)<=eta(b) pointwise. Their total masses differ: sum eta=1,
sum K=ell. Let psi be a nontrivial additive character and t!=0.
The top degree form of t Q(P(X),P(Y)) is

    t (X^(2D)+X^D Y^D+Y^(2D)).

It is squarefree over the algebraic closure: in the ratio X/Y its roots
are the D-th roots of the two distinct roots of Z^2+Z+1; they are nonzero
and simple because p does not divide 3D. The point at infinity is not a
root. It therefore defines a smooth zero-dimensional hypersurface in P^1.
Also p does not divide 2D. These facts hold for every lower coefficient
of P, not just random coefficients.

Deligne, La conjecture de Weil I, Theorem 8.4, printed pp.302–303, gives
for an n-variable polynomial with smooth top projective hypersurface and
degree d prime to p, the bound (d-1)^n p^(n/2) for its complete additive
sum. The parent read the original theorem at
https://www.numdam.org/item/PMIHES_1974__43__273_0.pdf . This application,
normalizations and scope still need independent audit.
For n=2, d=2D it proposes

    |eta_hat(t)| = |E psi(t Q(P(X),P(Y)))| <= (2D-1)^2/p.

Parseval therefore gives

    sum_b (eta(b)-1/p)^2 <= (2D-1)^4/p^2,
    sum_b K(b)^2 <= sum_b eta(b)^2
                  <= 1/p+(2D-1)^4/p^2.                         (1)

The omitted factor (p-1)/p only weakens the bound. We use formal degree;
no replacement modulo X^p-X is made. A theorem with a large right-hand
side is valid but uninformative. This does not bound all later depths.

## Statewise drift and root supply

The accepted exact laws are D_v=sum K^2-sum K A and D_m=sum K B.
Here sum B=s and sum B^2=2v, using the odd symmetry. Nonnegativity of B
and K<=eta, followed by Cauchy–Schwarz, gives

    0<=D_v<=1/p+(2D-1)^4/p^2,
    0<=D_m<=s/p + (2D-1)^2 sqrt(2v)/p.                         (2)

The lower bound for D_v is the separately proved orbit/graph result.
The root bound uses the actual beta distribution; it does not assume
uniform beta or take square roots of beta as computational inputs.
An auxiliary three-variable character sum is unnecessary.

Use the original W010 raw-attempt protocol modulo distinct p,q>3:
update only on the joint clean chart, paid no-op otherwise; record a
proper factor and freeze the map afterwards. At a fixed active state,
local raw drifts are multiplied by the other component's ell<=1.
Since D_v,D_m>=0, (2) bounds the stopped-and-frozen increments too.
After t raw attempts, the number of accepted updates is at most t and
D<=3^t. Fresh input means remain those of a fixed polynomial at that
realized state. No independence between survived prime histories is used.

Starting with v_0=(p-1)/p^2<=1/p, write

    V_t=(t+1)/p + (81^t-1)/(5p^2).

The inequality (2*3^j-1)^4<=16*81^j and a geometric sum propose

    E[v_t]<=V_t,                                               (3)
    E[m_k]<=(k+1)/p + (4/p) sum_(j=0)^(k-1) 9^j sqrt(2 V_j).    (4)

Equation (4) uses Jensen on sqrt(v_j), not survival-conditioned means.
The inactive contribution is zero. The expectation is over the entire
protocol, including failures and early factors, with their states frozen.
For k>=1 and 81^k<=p these imply the convenient bounds

    E[v_k]<=(k+6/5)/p,
    E[m_k]<=(k+1+0.5 sqrt(2k+2/5))/p.                          (5)

Indeed V_j<=(j+6/5)/p, and sum_(j<k)9^j=(9^k-1)/8<=sqrt(p)/8.
At k=0 use the original masses; no empty-sum ambiguity is needed.
These are O(k/p) bounds through D<=p^(1/4). Formal degree 3^k has not
produced exponential mean concentration in this regime.

## How this relates to success, and what it does not prove

At a fixed active state, a proper factor in the four anchor gcds requires
one of z,u,z-u,z+u to vanish at at least one component. A union bound at
p is at most

    2m + 2(m^2+v) <= 4m+2v,

and analogously at q. Sum these statewise probabilities over the actual
raw-attempt schedule, applying (3)-(4) to its stopped states. This gives
an O(k^2*(1/p+1/q)) training-success upper bound under 81^k<=min(p,q).
This is an upper bound with all full gcds included in the union; it is
not an exact success law. Earlier full-gcd stopping can only reduce the
set of tested events, provided the same update/no-op protocol is used.

A subsequent fresh sampled pin a=P(r), with proper gcd(a,N) recorded,
and one absorption update P(P-a), has local mean endpoint root mass
m+v when a is unrestricted. If the pin is clean-conditioned, do not use
this equality without its rejection factors. One can instead upper-bound
the unconditioned event for the attempted pin and its T fresh probes;
mark rejected/terminated paths inactive. The proposal is an
O((k^2+(T+1)(k+1))*(1/p+1/q)) full success bound for this SPECIFIED
training/one-pin/probe protocol in the same degree range. Its constants
and precise pin chart must be audited before acceptance.

This is a raw-budget envelope, not an expected-actual-work lower bound.
Training can stop early; k accepted layers can require more than k raw
attempts; an algorithm could try greater degrees or different probes.
Even acceptance of (1)-(5) would leave deeper cubic circuits open.
No application to the Jacobi-filtered training rule is assumed: it uses
a different beta distribution and can lose the sign of the drift.

## Constructive response

The smooth leading form is the exact obstruction being tested: it keeps
the sampled norm parameter almost flat at low degree, despite favorable
sampling bias. A possible escape must either enter greater circuit depth
with paid acquisition, change the leading form to acquire persistent
correlations, or lower detection work through a batch primitive. Existing
reciprocal and group-coherent maps have their own scoped failures and
cannot simply be relabeled as such an escape. The parent is developing
batch extraction alongside this calculation, without assuming a positive
review or an unexplained energy oracle.


Audit equations (1)-(5) and any actual-protocol success conclusion. Independently verify the ORIGINAL Deligne theorem8.4 (not a search snippet), top-form smoothness over algebraic closure even when D grows, normalized additive Fourier and Parseval constants, K<=eta, root Cauchy bound, adaptivity and stopped/frozen Jensen usage, degree cap, k=0 and k>=1 boundary, and pin-stage conditioning. Give a corrected explicit success bound for a fully specified one-pin chart if it follows. Do not promote raw-budget upper bound to actual-work lower bound or all-depth rejection. Parent is examining batch detection separately; do not undertake unrelated new algorithms or broad prior-art review. A symbolic counterexample to any claimed step is preferable to a broad finite sweep. Return scoped report and manifest.

Maintain a monic odd polynomial by its circuit, initially P(X)=X.

fixed raw-attempt budget. On the unit chart set

    beta=z^2+z*u+u^2,
    P_new=P^3-beta*P.                                           (1)

gcd(beta,N) would be an additional success channel and is not included
in the initial protocol. Every current map remains monic and odd;
zero is absorbing.

    F_beta(T)-F_beta(z)=(T-z)*(T-u)*(T+z+u),

It is a new acquisition rule; earlier polynomial/reciprocal envelopes

## Executable mechanism

Maintain a monic odd polynomial by its circuit, initially P(X)=X.
Take two fresh uniform residues modulo a remaining N=pq, p,q>3, and
evaluate z=P(r), u=P(s). Test z,u,z-u,z+u individually by gcd.
A proper gcd returns a factor. A full failure is a paid no-op under a
fixed raw-attempt budget. On the unit chart set

    beta=z^2+z*u+u^2,
    P_new=P^3-beta*P.                                           (1)

Beta need not be a unit. There is no division or square root. An optional
gcd(beta,N) would be an additional success channel and is not included
in the initial protocol. Every current map remains monic and odd;
zero is absorbing.

The exact identity is

    F_beta(T)-F_beta(z)=(T-z)*(T-u)*(T+z+u),
    F_beta(z)=F_beta(u)=F_beta(-z-u)=-z*u*(z+u).                   (2)

Thus the two actually sampled fibers z,u merge; their distinct negatives
merge into the opposite output. The third value -z-u also merges if it
is in the current image. Its presence is not assumed or supplied as an
oracle. The legal chart ensures the two outputs are nonzero and opposite.

Each update/probe stage needs a fixed number of modular operations.
Fresh parameter acquisition through depth k still costs O(k^2), and a
probe costs O(k); odd symmetry supplies negative anchors without extra
evaluations. The proposed saving would be a faster concentration of
nonzero fibers before a final absorption step, not cheap circuit evaluation.
The final step P*(P-a), a=P(r) from one paid fresh sample, can absorb a
mass-biased fiber; its cost and CRT success remain charged.

## Exact proposed sampler and drift

Fix one current odd map over F_p. Its output law mu is symmetric.
Write m=mu(0), let nu be the nonzero residual law, and set
s=sum nu, v=sum nu^2, q4=sum nu^4. Define Q(z,u)=z^2+z*u+u^2 and

    K(beta)=sum_(z,u!=0; z!=u; z!=-u; Q(z,u)=beta) nu(z)*nu(u),
    A(beta)=sum_(a!=0; a^2=beta) nu(a)^2,
    B(beta)=sum_(a!=0; a^2=beta) nu(a).

All ordered pairs are counted. Symmetry gives
sum K=s^2-2v=:ell. This is the raw legal probability; when ell=0
the conditional acquired-parameter law is undefined. When ell>0 it is
K(beta)/ell. The sampler measures no K.

The full off-diagonal collision gain at fixed beta has three disjoint
parts: K(beta), the opposite pairs A(beta), and the pairs involving zero
2m*B(beta). Also m_new=m+B(beta).
Symmetry implies B(beta)^2=2A(beta), including beta=0 or a nonsquare,
where both sides are zero. Subtracting the new atom square yields

    v_new-v=K(beta)-A(beta),
    m_new-m=B(beta).                                            (3)

Consequently the actual raw moments are

    E[1_legal*Delta v]=sum_beta K(beta)^2-sum_beta K(beta)*A(beta),
    E[1_legal*Delta m]=sum_beta K(beta)*B(beta).                  (4)

This supplies an executable bias toward the relevant quadratic-form
merger mass. Unlike the reciprocal sampler, it does not automatically
remove the two sampled heavy fibers into marked atoms. However the
root-removal term in (4) can still defeat a gain for a weighted law.
No universal monotonicity or reachable-law persistence is asserted.

For a flat symmetric residual support of size M, mass d=s/M per point,
every legal pair forces the four distinct ordered pairs
(z,u),(u,z),(-z,-u),(-u,-z). Thus K(beta)>=4d^2, while A(beta)<=2d^2.
This gives pointwise Delta v>=2d^2. The post-update law is generally
nonflat, so this one-step property cannot be iterated without proof.

## The actual uniform start, not an idealized distribution

Let epsilon=chi(-3), h=chi(3), C=p-epsilon-4 and D=3+h.
At uniform affine input nu=1/p on F_p^*, let k_beta=p^2*K(beta).
The standard nonsingular binary-quadratic count, followed by deletion
of zero coordinates and the two diagonals, proposes

    k_0=(p-1)*(1+epsilon),
    k_beta=C-D*chi(beta),              beta!=0,
    ell=(p-1)*(p-3)/p^2.                                     (5)

One can derive the count by completing the square:
4Q(z,u)=(2z+u)^2+3u^2. It is not a heuristic random-parameter law.
At nonzero beta, the original conic has p-epsilon points; remove
2*(1+chi(beta)) zero-coordinate points, 1+chi(beta/3) diagonal points,
and 1+chi(beta) opposite points. These deletions are disjoint for p>3.

Equations (3)-(5) give the proposed exact conditional means

    E[Delta v | legal]
      =[(p-1)*(1+epsilon)^2+C^2+D^2-C+D]/[p^2*(p-3)],
    E[Delta m | legal]=(C-D)/[p*(p-3)].                         (6)

In particular the first residual collision mass is 2/p+O(1/p^2),
and root mass is 2/p+O(1/p^2). No first-step exponent gain follows.
The potential difference is the subsequent weighted quadratic incidence,
not initial formal degree three or the number of planted pairs.

## Complete acquisition and recovery obligations

At a fixed map modulo N, fresh CRT samples are independent and the joint
clean probability is ell_p*ell_q. The raw local drifts in (4) multiply by
the other prime's ell in the no-op full-tape process. The accepted histories
are correlated across primes. Zero/full gcds and all unstarted stages stay
in the ledger; a clean-law formula is not a factoring success probability.
Every intermediate zero remains an endpoint zero, but extra coefficient
or derivative gcds would change the protocol.

A cheap-looking reservoir shortcut has an explicit debt. In a fixed pool
of input samples, applying the current global update to every stored value
merges at least the two distinct sampled classes on every accepted step.
Without replenishment, a pool of M distinct values supports at most M-1
such steps; if signed pairs are stored, the drop can be larger. Updating
all M values at every stage costs O(M*k). A fresh input evaluated through
the full circuit costs O(k). This closes only that literal pool scheme;
it is not a lower bound on lazy or structurally compressed acquisition.

# W010 — batch extraction from a trained map

## Executable detector, with global collisions handled

Freeze a current polynomial circuit P modulo distinct primes N=pq. Generate
2M fresh independent uniform inputs and evaluate their outputs modulo N.
Keep these conceptually as two lists of M for the probability proof, but
sort their union as canonical residues and remove EXACT modulo-N duplicates.
Let the resulting distinct values be c_1,...,c_L, L<=2M. Define

    F(T)=product_(i<=L)(T-c_i).

Build its monic product tree, formally differentiate, and multipoint-evaluate
F'(c_i) over Z/NZ. No factorial division or field assumption is needed.
For each i, gcd(F'(c_i),N) tests the product of every c_i-c_j, j!=i.
A proper gcd is a factor. If a full gcd occurs, recover a proper leaf by
splitting the other-factor product. Every leaf difference has gcd 1,p,or q,
never N, because exact global duplicates were removed. Thus a nonunit branch
cannot terminate at a full-gcd leaf. There is no assertion that a single
arbitrary branch works BEFORE this duplicate removal.

One concrete recovery implementation uses the sibling nodes on c_i's
root-to-leaf product-tree path: their polynomials partition all factors
except T-c_i. Evaluate these sibling polynomials at c_i and select a nonunit
one. If its gcd is N, recurse on its children. At each split, a unit child
can be discarded; a proper child immediately solves; a full child can be
followed. The sum of the evaluated polynomial degrees is O(L), including
finding the first sibling branch. This recovery is charged only after one
nonunit derivative value is detected, and stops at a proper factor.

Removing duplicate values preserves every useful pair: a pair with proper
gcd has different residues and both survive. It may remove useless full-gcd
pairs; that is precisely why it is needed. L<2 is a paid failure.

With a length-k sequential P circuit, fresh evaluation takes O(M(k+1))
modular operations. Tree construction and multipoint evaluation cost
quasilinear polynomial arithmetic with logarithmic tree overhead; fast
integer polynomial multiplication supplies the corresponding polylog factors
in M and log N. Include sorting, random bits, derivative, all gcds and O(M)
recovery. State the bit bound as

    (M(k+1)+M*polylog(M,N))*polylog(N),

or soft-O(M(k+1)*poly(log N)) when M<=N and the multiplication convention
is explicit. This is not an O(1) unbounded-integer operation model. An
implementation with schoolbook multiplication has a different cost.

## Exact first and second moments for useful pairs

At this fixed map, let mu_p,mu_q be the local output laws. Fresh outputs
have product law mu_p times mu_q by CRT. Define

    w_r=sum_a mu_r(a)^2,   t_r=sum_a mu_r(a)^3,  r=p,q,
    rho=w_p+w_q-2w_p*w_q.

For two independent outputs, rho is exactly the probability that their
difference has a proper gcd: equality at exactly one prime. Zero values
and their mass are included in w; this is not residual v alone.
Let Y count useful pairs across the original two independent M-lists.
Then E Y=M^2 rho. For a sampled output A, the conditional probability
of a useful partner is

    d(A)=mu_p(A_p)+mu_q(A_q)-2mu_p(A_p)*mu_q(A_q).

Writing kappa=E[d(A)^2], expansion gives

    kappa=t_p+t_q+4t_p*t_q+2w_p*w_q
          -4t_p*w_q-4w_p*t_q.                                 (1)

Disjoint list-pair events are independent. Two distinct events sharing one
endpoint have joint probability kappa. Hence exactly

    E Y^2=M^2 rho + 2M^2(M-1) kappa + M^2(M-1)^2 rho^2.          (2)

Paley–Zygmund at zero yields

    Pr(Y>0)>=M^2 rho^2/[rho+2(M-1)kappa+(M-1)^2 rho^2].          (3)

The detector tests at least these cross pairs, so it succeeds whenever Y>0.
A nonunit derivative is sufficient after exact duplicate handling.
No independence between all M^2 pairs is assumed.

## A sufficient birthday bound without flat weights

Suppose w_p,w_q<=1/2. Let T=w_p+w_q<=1. Then rho>=T/2.
Since t_r<=w_r^(3/2), and d<=mu_p+mu_q,

    kappa<=t_p+t_q+2w_p*w_q
          <=T^(3/2)+T^2/2
          <=(3/2)*T^(3/2) < 5*rho^(3/2).                       (4)

For any M>=rho^(-1/2), divide (2) by (E Y)^2. The diagonal term is at
most 1, the shared-endpoint term at most 10, and the disjoint term at
most 1. Thus

    Pr(detector finds a factor)>=1/12.                         (5)

No local L-infinity or uniform-support promise is added. The restriction
w_p,w_q<=1/2 is real: two almost globally constant output laws can have
tiny useful-pair probability arising from rare outliers, for which naive
birthday reasoning is inadequate. The exact (3) remains available there.
At a fixed map, a dyadic M schedule avoids receiving rho or the factors as
advice. It can reach the needed width at geometric total setup cost, with
fresh randomness at each width. This is a conditional detector guarantee;
acquiring the favorable map and any failed attempts still cost work.

## Quantitative target for cubic training

For W010, w_r=m_r^2+v_r. In the moderate-collision regime, rho is comparable
to w_p+w_q. At a fixed trained state the detector's leading evaluation cost
is roughly k/sqrt(rho), plus polynomial arithmetic. With a training cost
A_k, a candidate complete improvement must pay

    A_k + soft-O((k+1)/sqrt(rho)),

and include the probability of actually acquiring such a state. A mean
value of v across training histories does not supply that probability.
If the intended comparison is a sqrt(p) collision control, then for k>=1
one necessary scale target for this evaluator is

    rho substantially greater than k^2/p,
    A_k substantially less than sqrt(p),                      (6)

up to the explicitly retained bit/log factors and equal input assumptions.
This is a threshold comparison, not a lower bound on every implementation.
If useful collision mass grows only like k/p, batching costs roughly
sqrt(p*k), so mere linear growth loses to the identity-map control.
Even hypothetical k^2/p growth only cancels the increased probe depth at
this crude arithmetic scale. Growth faster than quadratic, a cheaper
trained evaluator, or asymmetric extraction outside this collision detector
would be required for the hoped-for exponent change.

The parent's norm-envelope derivation under separate review proposes

constrains early-depth claims; it does not close the deeper-depth branch
or supply an actual-work lower bound. The Jacobi selector is likewise a
separate detector modification, not a free improvement to (5).
